Extreme weather

Plan for the days when your customers need more power and your plants can deliver less.

  • Austin, Texas · 2017

    Deep Freeze

    In Austin, you have four years to prepare for the February 2021 freeze. When residents turn up the heat, how much of your fleet will still be running?

    Scenario details ↗

  • San Juan, Puerto Rico · 2000

    Hurricane Season

    A hurricane is coming to Puerto Rico. Several plants can lose output at once, and the oil you'll need during repairs gets more expensive.

    Scenario details ↗

  • Madrid, Spain · 2023

    Heatwave + Drought

    Spain's hottest days are hard on both sides of your grid. People turn up the air conditioning just as drought cuts hydro output and warm rivers limit reactor cooling.

    Scenario details ↗

  • Los Angeles, California · 2022

    Wildfire Emergency

    Wildfire will cut your Los Angeles utility's main power connection to a tenth of its usual capacity. What can you have ready by January 2025?

    Scenario details ↗

  • Lusaka, Zambia · 2012

    The River Runs Dry

    Zambia's Copperbelt mines draw power around the clock. The reservoir on the Zambezi starts full, but an El Niño drought is coming.

    Scenario details ↗

  • Delhi, India · 2018

    Delhi Summer

    Delhi's air conditioners need more power each summer. In the heat of 2024, coal and gas plants will produce less, and a late monsoon will prolong the shortage risk.

    Scenario details ↗

Rapid growth

A new customer wants power. How soon can you have it ready?

  • Manassas, Virginia · 2020

    Data Center Boom

    Manassas has six years to get ready for 100 MW of new data centers. They'll need power all night. What will you run after sunset?

    Scenario details ↗

  • Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania · 2006

    The Shale Boom

    A shale gas boom is coming to Pittsburgh. The fuel discount will end long before a new gas plant wears out.

    Scenario details ↗

  • Burlington, Vermont · 2005

    Across the Valley

    Buy three neighboring utilities by December 2014. Once the deals close, their customers expect you to keep the lights on too.

    Scenario details ↗

Energy transition

What will cover the hours your old power plants used to run?

  • San Francisco, California · 2020

    Carbon Fee

    San Francisco's coal plant has years left in it, but you pay a fee on its emissions. How soon can you afford to replace it?

    Scenario details ↗

  • Honolulu, Hawaii · 2003

    Paradise

    Honolulu has plenty of sun and wind. On a calm night, you're paying for imported oil. There's no neighboring grid to buy power from.

    Scenario details ↗

  • San Francisco, California · 2002

    Rise of Renewables

    Wind and solar are getting cheaper in California. Waiting could save you money, but new factories will need power before long.

    Scenario details ↗

  • Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania · 1980

    The End of an Era

    Two coal plants power your Pittsburgh utility. They're getting older, and a replacement can take years to build. Your customers can switch suppliers sooner than that.

    Scenario details ↗

  • Paris, France · 2023

    Sudden Nuclear Shutdown

    Your largest reactor supplies much of your Paris utility's power. Sometime during your five-year term it will shut down and stay offline.

    Scenario details ↗

  • Johannesburg, South Africa · 2016

    Load Shedding

    Coal plants in your Johannesburg utility are breaking down faster than they can be repaired. Diesel can keep the lights on, if you can pay the fuel bill.

    Scenario details ↗

  • Kyiv, Ukrainian SSR · 1986

    Chernobyl: Recovery

    In March 1986, all four Chernobyl reactors are producing electricity. A month from now, all four will be offline. Part of your job is paying for the cleanup.

    Scenario details ↗

Legacy campaign

Start with 100 customers in 1882. Each generation takes over the utility you built in the last one.

  • A fictional California utility · 1882

    First Light (1882–1901)

    It's 1882. You own one small coal plant and sell electricity to 100 customers. Can you get their payments to cover the cost of keeping the plant running?

    Scenario details ↗

  • A fictional California utility · 1902

    Beyond the Dynamo (1902–1921)

    More people want electricity from the company you started in First Light. How many new customers can the old plants serve before you have to borrow for another one?

    Scenario details ↗

  • A fictional California utility · 1922

    Affordable Growth (1922–1941)

    Your California utility has more customers now. They need enough new capacity to meet rising demand, at a rate they can still afford.

    Scenario details ↗

  • A fictional California utility · 1942

    Everybody Plugs In (1942–1961)

    More California homes and businesses are plugging in. Halfway through your term you'll need spare power on top of what they're already using.

    Scenario details ↗

  • A fictional California utility · 1962

    The Power You Don't Build (1962–1981)

    The oil shocks of the 1970s are coming. If your customers can use less electricity, your California utility can buy less fuel.

    Scenario details ↗

  • A fictional California utility · 1982

    The Price of Power (1982–2001)

    Regional power has helped supply your California utility. From July 2000, the northern connection won't be able to bring in as much.

    Scenario details ↗

  • A fictional California utility · 2002

    The Sun Moves the Peak (2002–2021)

    Solar can cover a sunny California afternoon. This generation's goal is to serve 99.5% of evening demand, when solar output is falling.

    Scenario details ↗

  • A fictional California utility · 2022

    Renew the Grid (2022–2041)

    Which oil plants are still running after seven generations? It's 2022, and any you kept from 2000 or earlier will need to retire as California's demand grows.

    Scenario details ↗

  • A fictional California utility · 2042

    A Different Kind of Growth (2042–2061)

    Your last twenty years come with one carbon budget. Every tonne your California utility emits in 2042 counts toward the same total as a tonne in 2061.

    Scenario details ↗
